summary: DV4 sits within the contested Lanarkshire AI Growth Zone. APRS and local campaigners criticise the lack of transparency about the zone's extent, the Green Belt location, the adequacy of EIA screening, and headline jobs figures. DataVita says it revised the design after May-June consultation and now proposes a £75m site-specific community fund, local-contract targets, native hedgerow and heat-recovery discussions. These remain developer commitments until the validated application and any legal agreement are published.

principal_concerns.concern: Transparency: the extent of the AI Growth Zone has not been published; APRS obtained the DV4 screening report only via a council request and notes the screening opinion was published a month after the decision
Adequacy of EIA screening: screening determined 'not required' in nine working days on a report APRS describes as containing no layout diagram of the proposed development
Green Belt loss and cumulative impact with DV6, ILI's Aurelius proposal and multiple energy developments south and east of Chapelhall
Jobs claims: FoI response indicates >90% of the 3,400 zone jobs are construction/indirect/induced, with induced jobs potentially arising outside Lanarkshire or Scotland

claimed_local_benefits.benefit: £75m DV4 community fund over 15 years, with allocation and governance still to be published
Target for at least 40% of capital contracts to be placed with local businesses
Heat-recovery discussions with University Hospital Monklands and BioCity

AI Growth Zone-wide Community Investment Fund of up to £543m over 15 years at full operation (£36m+/year), plus £1m/year HFD charitable giving; this is not a DV4-only sum and must not be added to the proposed £75m DV4 fund
Excess heat from cooling systems to be redirected to University Hospital Monklands

stakeholder_positions.position: Opposed/critical: transparency, Green Belt, screening adequacy, jobs and renewable-energy deliverability critiques
Welcomed the AI Growth Zone designation
Designated and promotes the zone; 'AI Growth Zones are bringing generation-defining opportunity' (Technology Secretary Liz Kendall)

notes: Developer consultation events: 12 May 2026 (Mount Pleasant Community Centre), 2 June 2026 (venue TBC), 4 June 2026 (Mount Pleasant Community Centre). APRS reminds residents comments at developer events are not formal representations. Application-submission benefits are developer-stated; no section 75 agreement or other enforceable mechanism was available by 3 September 2026.
